title: Flow factory job state machine
about: The single table of job states, events, guards and transitions. check_transitions.py validates it and derives the entry and exit lists; transitions.md is generated from it.

conventions.precedence: Within one (state, event), when several rows match, the row with the lowest precedence number applies. Ties are errors.
conventions.guard: An object fact -> true/false. All listed facts must hold. A fact the guard omits is not read by that row.
conventions.stay: A row with "stay": true leaves the job in its state and applies its effects.
conventions.computed_targets: "to": "resume_state" or "blocked_stage" moves the job to the value a parking row recorded. "resume" lists the possible targets, and the checker compares it with the "records" of the rows in "resume_from" ("*" means every row entering the state that records the value).
conventions.no_move_ok: An event's no_move_ok entry lets the job stay in the listed states when no row matches and the facts agree with "when". Each entry has a written reason.
conventions.event_order: Within one engine pass, events are applied in event_order. A job that left its state ignores the later events of that pass, and a stage result for a stage it left is refused with that stage's lease. A change that a github_change reported stays pending until a row whose guard reads its fact as true has applied, and the sync raises github_change again in each later pass while a change is pending. So a change seen in the same pass as a move, or under a row with a lower precedence number, is applied in a later pass, in the job's new state. One exception comes before the order, and it is data: pass_first names the event, the facts and the rows applied before every event of event_order. When the sync of the pass shows the job's PR merged by a person (pr_merged_by_person), row 54 is applied first, so a cancel, reject or other person event of the same pass cannot end a merged job as cancelled or rejected.
conventions.slots: A job takes a slot when a stage of it launches and it holds none; row 66w keeps the launch waiting while no slot is free. The job keeps the slot while it stays in active states other than queued and ready. The engine frees it whenever the job enters ready, a parked state or a terminal state, so rows do not repeat that effect. Rows 2 and 36 also read slot_free, so a job does not leave queued, or undo ready to go to sync, while no slot is free. Row 55 does not read it: approve keeps the PR marked ready, and the approver's launch waits for a slot at row 66w. Row 36u does not read it either: the undo of ready has already run, so the job goes to sync and its launch waits at row 66w.
conventions.ready_and_drafts: A PR is marked ready only in ready, in the phase 2 states approve, merging and waiting_ci, and in waiting_operator while the job waits for the undo of ready (pending_undo_ready). Every move out of ready, approve, merging or waiting_ci to another non-terminal state first runs gh pr ready --undo and removes the flow:ready label, and such a row lists 'undo of ready' in its writes. That undo is a blocking write: when its key resolves to confirm, rows 40, 40f, 40g, 40j, 40l, 40p, 40r, 40t, 40x and 40y park the job in waiting_operator first, and row 40h holds every github_change there until the undo is confirmed or observed. After it, the job resumes into ready with the PR no longer marked, and the held event is replayed there. If the replay does not move the job, ready_mark_missing is true and row 36u sends it to sync at the next sync_tick, in the same pass or the next, and row 31 marks the PR ready again.
conventions.run_by: Each active state names what runs it: the engine inline, an engine directive, a judge with no tools, or a claude -p worker. check_transitions.py requires launch_due, lease_expired and stage_failed in exactly the states run by a directive, judge or worker, stage_succeeded in those run by a directive or worker, worker_parked and question_stored in worker states, and github_change, person_cancel and person_rebuild in every non-terminal state.
conventions.writes: A row's 'writes' lists the blocking GitHub writes it makes, per from-state where they differ. blocking_write_confirm is derived from them: it can be true only when the row that would win with it false lists a write, and then a row that parks in waiting_operator recording resume_state wins. The writes of a review, rework or resolve result are made before the result's row applies, so row 20b lists them too. Every engine push is preceded by the protected and config-loading check (rules.push_check); on a violation row 21f freezes the job in needs_human and nothing is pushed.
conventions.rules_and_expectations: 'rules' and 'expectations' hold, as data, the rules the design states in prose. check_transitions.py fails when a row breaks one: for example when a person action acts without its confirmation, when a blocking write has no confirm park, or when a person's cancel, merge or rejection does not end the job.
conventions.person_events_elsewhere: A person event raised for a job in a state outside that event's occurs_in list is refused without a move: the subcommand exits 3 with EVENT_REFUSED=<event> state=<state>, and a trusted comment gets no reaction other than a status note naming the state. The checker requires an occurs_in list for every person event.

pass_first.why: When the sync of a pass shows the job's PR merged by a person, row 54 applies before every event of event_order, so a cancel, reject or other person event of the same pass cannot end a merged job as cancelled or rejected. The checker requires that, in every state where github_change occurs, a row listed here wins whenever the 'when' holds.

person_confirmation.why: An always-ask person subcommand acts only with the confirmation the engine checks: from a terminal, the job id typed back on the controlling terminal; from inside a Claude session, a session whose recorded permission mode is default, where tier-gate's always-ask shows the person the command with its arguments (design person_channels items 3 and 4). In auto mode, or when the mode is unknown, the session is refused; rows 69a to 69h refuse without the confirmation.

blocking_write.why: A blocking write whose tier key resolves to confirm waits as a pending intent in waiting_operator (design github_writes_and_tiers).

ready_mark.why: conventions.ready_and_drafts. A confirm park taken where the PR is marked ready resumes into ready, where the held event is replayed. Only rows 41, 41e and 41k may resume a job into a marked state; they follow the undo of ready, so the job enters ready with ready_mark_missing set, and row 36u then sends it to sync, where row 31 marks the PR ready again. A row may record a marked state only from a marked from-state.

push_check.why: The protected and config-loading check runs right before every engine push. Like blocking_write_confirm, prepush_protected_failed is derived: it can be true only when the row that wins with it false lists a push. Then a row that moves the job to needs_human without a push must win (row 21f), so a worker's commit to a protected or config-loading path never reaches the remote, where a workflow file would run with the repository's secrets.

records_as_if.why: After approval the job enters the state row 13 would have entered.
After approval the job enters the state the stage's own row would have entered.

issue_changed.meaning: issue_digest differs from baseline_digest. baseline_digest is written in one place only: row 66i, when the engine writes in/issue.md for an intake launch. Every row that enters intake sets baseline_pending, and row 66i clears it. While no baseline exists or baseline_pending is set (including a waiting_operator park taken at that intake launch, and a needs_human park entered from queued), the fact is false. It is not read in queued.

untrusted_edit.meaning: Since vouch_at, the title or body was edited by an editor who is untrusted or unknown, or a comment in the spec-input set (a needs-info answer or a /flow-factory spec comment) was edited after it joined the set by an editor other than a trusted account that is not a machine account. A re-vouched reply from an author without write access counts at the body it had at the re-vouch, so a later edit by that author is an untrusted edit. Cleared by a trusted retry or a label re-add that re-vouches it.

build_started.meaning: Set by row 13 or row 15 when the job first enters build. Never cleared, so it says the job had reached build, whatever stage a later park recorded (row 52h reads it in needs_human).

needs_info_answer.meaning: Since the factory's needs-info marker, a reply arrived that counts as a needs-info answer: it names or quotes a needs-info question id (NI-<k>), and its author is trusted (write access or higher, design person_channels item 5). An issue author without write access is not trusted: their reply counts only after a trusted retry (row 8r). Such replies are in the spec-input set, so this implies issue_changed. Trusted discussion that names no question id is not an answer and never moves issue_digest.

untrusted_needs_info_answer.meaning: Since the needs-info marker, a reply that names a needs-info question id arrived from an author who is not trusted, the issue author included, and no trusted retry has re-vouched it. It is not in the spec-input set.

cancel_signal.meaning: The queue label was removed, or the issue was closed, by an actor with write access or higher, as the collaborator permission endpoint reports it (trust rules for bot and App actors: design person_channels item 5). A label removal or a close by anyone else is not a cancel: a removal posts a status note and re-adds nothing, and the job keeps running; a close is untrusted_close. When the same sync also shows the PR merged by a person, row 54 outranks every row that reads this fact, because merging a PR that says 'Closes #N' also closes the issue.

untrusted_close.meaning: The issue was closed by an actor without write access, it is still closed, and the PR, if any, was not merged. The issue author can close their own issue, so such a close parks the job (row 53u) instead of cancelling it.

pr_exists.meaning: The job's PR exists, open or merged. The job's PR is the one whose number the engine recorded when it created it (row 21), with its head in this repository; a PR from a fork, or one the engine did not create, is never the job's PR, whatever its branch name.

pr_merged_by_person.meaning: GitHub reports the job's PR as MERGED and the factory did not merge it.

pr_closed_by_person.meaning: GitHub reports the job's PR as closed without a merge, and the factory did not close it.

foreign_head_change.meaning: The PR head moved to a commit the factory did not push.

slot_free.meaning: A worker slot is free and open jobs are below maxOpenJobs. Read by rows that leave queued or ready; launches read slot_available.

slot_available.meaning: The job already holds a slot, or one is free: fewer than concurrency jobs hold a slot.

dependency_open.meaning: An issue named in 'Depends on' or 'Blocked by' is still open.

tier_confirm_blocking.meaning: A tier key of a blocking write left on the job's path resolves to confirm. The keys by stage: prepare: issueAssign, issueUpdate; open_pr: push, prCreate, issueUpdate; review, rework, sync, resolve: push, issueUpdate; ready: issueUpdate; approve (phase 2): issueUpdate, for the undo of ready when the job leaves phase 2.

executor_can_confirm.meaning: The executor running next can get a person's confirm at write time: an interactive executor is present (interactive_presence's heartbeat record, without the P14 condition, because confirming holds no question) and its record shows the session's permission mode as default, where tier-gate's always-ask on 'flow-factory.sh confirm <intent>' shows the person the stored literal. False for the headless runner, false in auto mode, and false when the mode is unknown, whatever P9 shows: in auto mode a confirm item parks before launch and a person confirms it in a terminal. No classifier decision makes it true.

blocking_write_confirm.meaning: Derived, not observed. The row that would win for this event with this fact false lists a blocking write in its 'writes' (push, PR create or edit, review or resolution marker, replies, the ready mark or its undo, label, assignment) whose tier key resolves to confirm, and the write's intent has no confirmation. The engine evaluates the table with the fact false first, and check_transitions.py derives it the same way (rules.blocking_write).

park_tier_confirm.meaning: The job is in waiting_operator for reason tier_confirm (row 40b). False when it waits for a pending intent (rows 40, 40f, 40g, 40j, 40l, 40p, 40r, 40t, 40x and 40y).

intent_effect_observed.meaning: The pending intent's effect is visible on GitHub or the remote (a person ran the write).

intent_key_not_confirm.meaning: The pending intent's tier key no longer resolves to confirm.

pending_undo_ready.meaning: The job parked here from ready, approve, merging or waiting_ci (rows 40 from merging, 40f, 40g, 40j, 40l, 40p, 40r, 40t, 40x and 40y): the PR is still marked ready, and the pending intent is the undo of ready that every move out of those states needs.

pending_intent_stale.meaning: The pending intent is a push, or a marker, reply or comment written for the head before a foreign push, so the foreign push made it stale.

unvouched_session_action.meaning: An always-ask person subcommand (approve-spec, confirm, feedback, rework, retry, reject, cancel, rebuild) lacks the confirmation the engine checks. Outside a Claude session, the confirmation is a controlling terminal and the job id typed on it. Inside a session (CLAUDECODE set, or a claude process among its ancestors), the subcommand is confirmed only when the session's heartbeat record shows permission mode default, where tier-gate's always-ask shows the person the command with its arguments; in auto mode, or when the mode is unknown or the interactive probe group is stale, the fact is true and the engine refuses. False for a trusted comment.

attempts_exhausted.meaning: attempt has reached 2 for the current stage.

tree_dirty.meaning: The job's worktree has changes that the finalize commit does not take.

group_gone.meaning: The stage's process group is confirmed gone after SIGTERM and SIGKILL.

orphan_group_alive.meaning: A process group of an earlier stage of this job, which the engine killed when a row left that stage, was not confirmed gone and is still alive.

failure_needs_person.meaning: prepare failed in a way a retry cannot change: bootstrap failed, a copy entry was refused, or the tree is dirty.

prelaunch_protected_failed.meaning: The protected-path check that runs before every launch found a violation, or the job clone's git config differs from the copy the engine wrote at prepare (worktrees_ports_bootstrap_auth, Engine git commands).

prepush_protected_failed.meaning: The protected and config-loading check that runs right before an engine push (the merge-base protected-path check over merge-base..HEAD and the comparison of the job clone's git config with the copy the engine wrote at prepare) found a violation. Derived the same way as blocking_write_confirm: it can be true only when the row that would win with it false lists a push (rules.push_check).

clone_config_changed.meaning: The job clone's .git/config, or .git/config.worktree when present, differs from the copy the engine wrote at prepare. The engine compares the files without running git (worktrees_ports_bootstrap_auth, Engine git commands).

probes_stale.meaning: The platform probe record does not match 'claude --version'. Only worker and judge launches read it; engine directives go on. A failed automatic re-run of the environment probe group is not this fact: while it fails, the engine raises no launch_due event for any job (events.launch_due).

interactive_presence.meaning: An interactive executor is present and holds questions. Presence comes from the heartbeat record factory/executors/interactive.json (heartbeat_at, the claude pid, the session's permission mode and its P9 and P14 results), which every 'next' and 'wait' call of the session refreshes: presence counts while the claude pid is alive, the claude pid is no lease's child, and heartbeat_at is younger than presenceTimeoutSeconds (300), which is longer than the poll interval of 'await'. A 'wait' that exits to wake the session therefore leaves presence in place while the session asks. The record must also say P14 passed.

held_question.meaning: A stored blocking question of this stage's worker is in 'held' state: the worker is alive and polling await.

question_already_answered.meaning: The resolve worker parked on a file whose question for this conflict_base_sha and hunk hash was already answered.

spec_approval_required.meaning: Effective risk is high (intake said high, or RISK is high or unknown), or specApproval is 'all'.

spec_change_needs_approval.meaning: The stage changed spec_hash, and approval is required (risk high, specApproval 'all', or an approval was already given).

approval_matches_current.meaning: The approval names the current spec_hash and, when resume_state is gate, the current head H. Both are the values the sync of this pass computed from the PR head before it applied any event, so a push seen in the same pass as the approval is already in them.

protected_change.meaning: The gate's protected check found a violation, the goal freeze hash changed, or the job clone's git config differs from the copy the engine wrote at prepare.

gate_commands_missing.meaning: gate.commands at origin/<base> is empty or unreadable.

gate_pass.meaning: The gate commands passed at H.

diff_risk_needs_approval.meaning: Diff risk over merge-base..H is high, specApproval is 'high', and no approval is recorded.

valid_review_at_head.meaning: An engine-posted review marker of the current round has head_end == H, or one was carried to H.

ledger_passes.meaning: The review ledger passes at H (review_routing_and_markers item 4).

gate_at_head.meaning: A passing gate record exists for the current HEAD, with HEAD == remote == headRefOid.

marker_agreement.meaning: Among markers whose author /flow:merge would trust, the latest of each kind is engine-posted, matched by the id recorded in the ledger, and its body still has the sha256 recorded when the engine posted it (review_routing_and_markers item 5).

escalated.meaning: The review's ESCALATED list is not empty.

head_moved.meaning: The review stage pushed fix-forward commits, so HEAD moved.

base_moved.meaning: ls-remote of the base differs from gate.base_sha.

merge_conflict.meaning: Merging the moved base gave a conflict.

conflict_protected.meaning: The conflict touches a protected or config-loading path.

trusted_changes_requested.meaning: A CHANGES_REQUESTED review was posted after the ready marker, at the current head, by a trusted author that is not a machine account, or by a machine account and then confirmed by a person (person_channels item 5).

ready_mark_missing.meaning: The job is in ready, but the PR is no longer marked ready: the job resumed into ready after the undo of ready ran or was observed (rows 41, 41e, 41k), and the replayed event did not move it.

via_comment.meaning: The person event came from a trusted '/flow-factory <command>' comment posted after the factory's latest marker, not from a terminal subcommand or the interactive executor.

retry_by_triage_only.meaning: The retry came from a /flow-factory retry comment whose author has triage access but not write access. Such a retry only re-vouches text from someone without write access: a needs-info reply (row 8r) or an untrusted edit (row 44d). It resumes no other park: rows 8t (needs_info, no untrusted reply waits) and 44t (needs_human) refuse it.

open_questions_remaining.meaning: After this answer, the job still has an open blocking question.

resolve_repeat_blocked.meaning: needs_human reason is resolve_repeat, and the base has not moved past conflict_base_sha.

blocked_before_spec.meaning: needs_human's recorded blocked_stage is intake or prepare: intake has not accepted the current issue, or prepare has not finished.

automerge_enabled.meaning: Phase 2. The user-only switch is on, the repository is allowlisted, and the outside-session runner (no --no-merge) is the executor of this pass.

automerge_switch_off.meaning: Phase 2. The user-only autoMerge.enabled switch is off, or the repository is not in autoMerge.repos. Unlike automerge_enabled, it does not depend on which executor runs the pass.

automerge_tried_at_head.meaning: Phase 2. For the current head, row 55 or row 61 wrote its approve-entry record when it moved the job to approve, the approver wrote approve-<H>.json, or a failed pre-check record exists. So approve is entered at most once per head.

precheck_passes.meaning: Phase 2. The eligibility pre-check at H finds no category and no unverified item.

checks_pending.meaning: Phase 2. Checks at H are still running, or the base moved and the runner merged it, re-gated and pushed H2.

merge_done.meaning: Phase 2. The PR is MERGED with headRefOid equal to the --match-head-commit SHA.

checks_all_success.meaning: Phase 2. Every check at H is SUCCESS, and at least one exists.

check_failed.meaning: Phase 2. A check at H failed.

approval_valid_at_head.meaning: Phase 2. The approver's APPROVE and the gate record both name the current head.

ci_timeout.meaning: Phase 2. ciTimeoutSeconds passed since the job entered waiting_ci.

fact_dependencies.why: A merged PR exists and is not closed-without-merge.
A closed PR exists.
Only a PR has a head to move.
A needs-info answer is in the spec-input set, so it moves issue_digest.
A merge happens only when the base moved.
A protected conflict is a conflict.
A protected violation is a gate failure.
An empty or unreadable command list is a gate failure.
All checks succeeded.
A merged PR has no pending merge checks.
Only a pending intent has an effect.
Only a pending intent has a key.
needs_human has one reason, and resolve_repeat records blocked_stage sync, which comes after build.
A queued job has not built and has no PR.
These states come after the first entry to build.
These states come after open_pr created the PR.
Judges have no tools and do not touch the worktree.
Rows 9, 9a and 9r record blocked_stage intake.
approve runs only under the outside-session runner, which cannot confirm at write time (auto_merge_phase2 item 2).
untrusted_close is defined only for a PR that was not merged.
A park from ready is a write-time park, and ready comes after build.
automerge_enabled needs the switch on.
The undo of ready already ran, so no row needs it again.
Only a pending push, marker, reply or comment is tied to a head. A tier_confirm park has no intent, and the undo of ready is not tied to a head.

queued.meaning: The issue carries the queue label and the job waits for a slot and for its dependencies.

intake.meaning: The intake judge (no tools) reads in/issue.md and returns ACCEPT, REJECT or NEEDS_INFO.

prepare.meaning: Engine directive: branch, goal id, job clone, ignore rules, io directory, ports for the job's slot, assignment, label and bootstrap.

spec.meaning: Worker: specification-capture writes the Specification and Factory criteria sections with this job's marker.

build.meaning: Worker: /flow:start in factory mode builds the change and achieves the job's goal.

open_pr.meaning: Worker writes out/pr.md; the engine pushes and opens or edits the draft PR.

gate.meaning: Engine directive: base-branch gate commands, protected-path check, goal freeze and diff risk at head H.

review.meaning: Worker: /flow:review in factory mode; the engine pushes fix-forward commits and posts the review and resolution markers.

rework.meaning: Worker: /flow:address in factory mode; the engine pushes and posts the resolution marker and replies.

sync.meaning: Engine directive: compare the base, merge it when it moved, and check the ready conditions when it did not.

resolve.meaning: Worker: /flow:resolve finishes a base merge that has a non-protected conflict.

ready.meaning: The PR is marked ready and waits for a person to merge it or send it back.

approve.meaning: Phase 2. The approver judge (no tools) returns APPROVE or ESCALATE for head H.

merging.meaning: Phase 2. Engine directive run by the outside-session runner: it checks whether the PR is already MERGED at H, otherwise merges with --match-head-commit H.

needs_info.meaning: The factory asked the issue for information and waits for an answer, an edit or a retry.

needs_spec_approval.meaning: A high-risk or changed specification waits for a person's approval, change request or rejection.

waiting_operator.meaning: A blocking GitHub write needs a confirm-tier approval, either before launch (tier_confirm) or at write time (pending_intent).

needs_human.meaning: The factory cannot go on without a person: an answer, a retry, feedback, a push, a rejection or a cancel.

waiting_ci.meaning: Phase 2. The merge waits for the checks at head H. The PR stays marked ready, because the merge needs a PR that is not a draft; this is the only parked state that keeps it so.

merged.meaning: The PR was merged, by a person or (phase 2) by the runner.

rejected.meaning: The job was rejected by intake or by a person.

cancelled.meaning: The job was cancelled: by a person, by removing the label, by closing the issue, or by closing the PR without merging.

issue_labelled.meaning: The queue label was added to an open issue. Only the creation row reads it.

sync_tick.meaning: One pass of 'next', after the GitHub sync and after any github_change events of that pass were applied.

no_move_ok.reason: No slot is free, so the job waits in the queue.
A dependency is still open, so the job waits in the queue.
The base has not moved and auto-merge is off, so ready waits for a person.
The base has not moved and auto-merge already ran for this head, so ready waits for a person.
The base moved but no slot is free; sync starts when one frees.
The pending intent still needs a confirm; rows 41 and 41e handle the confirm and the observed effect.
A confirm-tier key is still on the path and no executor can confirm at write time.
The checks are still within ciTimeoutSeconds.

github_change.meaning: The GitHub sync saw a change to the issue (title, body, labels, state, comments that are not /flow-factory commands), to the PR (state, head, reviews, comments) or to the base branch. Trusted '/flow-factory <command>' comments arrive as the matching person_* event instead.

no_move_ok.reason: Nothing queued reacts to changed: ordinary discussion and edits are read when intake launches. A queued job has no PR, so a PR merge or close is not read here.
Nothing these states react to changed; ordinary discussion never moves issue_digest.
Nothing these states react to changed; the stage's own result moves the job.
Ready waits for a person; base moves are handled on sync_tick.
Nothing these phase 2 states react to changed; the judge's or the merge directive's result moves the job.
No needs-info answer, trusted edit, /flow-factory spec comment or push arrived; trusted discussion that names no question id does not count.
The job waits for the approval decision.
The job waits for a confirm, a tier change or the observed effect.

needs_human waits for a person. An untrusted edit, an issue change or an untrusted close moves nothing here: the person rows read them, refuse an answer, a retry or feedback while they last (rows 44u, 44v, 44w, 44z, 45v, 45w and 45z), and a retry after an edit or a change goes back through intake (rows 44c and 44d). A push while one of them lasts is recorded by row 52hs.
Checks are still pending at H.

launch_due.meaning: The engine is about to start the state's judge, worker or directive: the first launch in this state, or a relaunch after rows 39, 39d, 39l, 39ld and 52e. A relaunch after row 52e counts no attempt. The launch takes a slot when the job holds none. While the environment probe group fails its automatic re-run (phasing, Phase 0: PAUSED probes_failed=environment), the engine raises no launch_due event for any job, so no judge, worker or engine directive starts and no attempt is counted; the other events go on.

stage_succeeded.meaning: The state's worker or directive exited without error and its post-stage checks passed (finalize commit, clean tree, required outputs, the stage postconditions in design 'stages'). A failed check is stage_failed.

stage_failed.meaning: The stage ended with a non-usage-limit error, a malformed judge result, a refused finalize, or a failed post-stage check. A stage timeout counts here; the launcher suspends the timeout while a question is held, up to askHoldSeconds. A usage-limit result is not an event: it sets paused_until.

lease_expired.meaning: The stage's lease heartbeat is older than leaseSeconds with no result reported.

worker_parked.meaning: The worker exited after await printed PARK for a blocking question (no interactive presence, askHoldSeconds passed, or askHoldPolls reached). A held question whose worker is still alive is not this event.

question_stored.meaning: The worker stored a Blocking: yes question with flow-question.sh add --issue N and started polling await.

judge_needs_info.meaning: The intake judge returned NEEDS_INFO with questions.

judge_approve.meaning: Phase 2. The approver judge returned APPROVE for H.

judge_escalate.meaning: Phase 2. The approver judge returned ESCALATE.

person_answer.meaning: A person answered a stored question of this job ('answer <qid>'); in needs_spec_approval, the answer is a change request with redraft text; in needs_info, it names a needs-info question id. Channels: a terminal subcommand, a trusted '/flow-factory <command>' comment posted after the factory's latest marker, or the interactive executor: a held question's `--choice` after AskUserQuestion, and `--text` only in default permission mode, through tier-gate's ask.

person_approve_spec.meaning: A person approved the specification ('approve-spec'). Channels: a terminal subcommand, a trusted '/flow-factory <command>' comment posted after the factory's latest marker, or the interactive executor in default permission mode, through tier-gate's ask.

person_confirm.meaning: A person confirmed a pending intent by id ('flow-factory.sh confirm <intent>'). Terminal or interactive executor only.

person_retry.meaning: A person asked for a retry ('retry'). Every retry re-vouches: vouch_at = now. Channels: a terminal subcommand, a trusted '/flow-factory <command>' comment posted after the factory's latest marker, or the interactive executor in default permission mode, through tier-gate's ask.

person_rework.meaning: A person sent the PR back with text, from ready or from the phase 2 states approve, merging and waiting_ci, where the PR is also marked ready ('flow-factory.sh rework <text>' in a terminal, or a trusted '/flow-factory rework <text>' comment after the ready marker). Channels: a terminal subcommand, a trusted '/flow-factory <command>' comment posted after the factory's latest marker, or the interactive executor in default permission mode, through tier-gate's ask.

person_feedback.meaning: A person gave feedback with 'flow-factory.sh feedback'. Terminal or interactive executor only.

person_reject.meaning: A person rejected the job ('reject'). Channels: a terminal subcommand, a trusted '/flow-factory <command>' comment posted after the factory's latest marker, or the interactive executor in default permission mode, through tier-gate's ask.

person_cancel.meaning: A person cancelled the job ('cancel'). Channels: a terminal subcommand, a trusted '/flow-factory <command>' comment posted after the factory's latest marker, or the interactive executor in default permission mode, through tier-gate's ask.

expectations.why: A person's confirmed cancel ends the job from every non-terminal state.
Row 54 records a person's merge from every state that can have a PR, and outranks a cancel signal or close seen in the same sync.
A close without merge by a person ends the job as cancelled (row 53c).
A removed queue label, or an issue closed by someone with write access, cancels the job (row 53b).
An issue closed by someone without write access parks the job instead of ending it (row 53u); from a state where the PR is marked ready the undo may wait for a confirm first.
In waiting_operator, an untrusted close parks the job unless the undo of ready waits (row 53uw).
An untrusted edit stops the job until a trusted retry re-vouches it (row 51b).
A trusted issue change before build sends the job back through intake (rows 50 and 18).
A trusted issue change after build parks the job for a retry, which goes back through intake (row 51).
A push the factory did not make sends a job with a PR to gate (row 52).
A push the factory did not make, seen before the job reached open_pr, moves the worktree branch to the new head (row 52e).
A trusted request for changes sends back a PR that is marked ready, in ready and in phase 2 (row 37); plan decision 'Sending a ready PR back'.
The rework comment and the rework subcommand send back a PR that is marked ready (rows 37b and 37c).
Feedback sends back a PR that is marked ready (row 37d).
A person's confirmed rejection ends the job in each parked state that offers it (rows 19, 42 and 48).
An approval of the current spec resumes the job into the recorded stage (row 15).
A trusted needs-info answer sends the job back to intake (row 8).
A needs-info reply from someone without write access waits for a retry from triage access or higher (row 8u).
A retry from triage access only re-vouches text from someone without write access; it resumes no other park (row 44t).
A retry from triage access re-vouches an untrusted edit and goes back through intake (row 44d).
While an issue closed by someone without write access stays closed, a retry or feedback does not resume the job (rows 44z and 45z).
While an issue closed by someone without write access stays closed, an answer is recorded but does not resume the job (row 44u).
A confirm-tier key on the job's path parks the job before anything is spent when no executor can confirm (row 40b).
The protected-path and clone-config check runs before every launch, the merge directive's included (row 43p).
A changed clone config parks the job without any engine git command in the clone (rows 43x and 43y).
A job does not leave queued while no slot is free (row 2).
A job does not undo ready to go to sync while no slot is free (row 36).
A job left in ready with the PR no longer marked goes to sync, which marks it ready again (row 36u).
approve is entered at most once per head (row 55 records the entry).
A trusted foreign marker parks a job in sync while the base is unchanged (row 31b).
A retry from triage access in needs_info only re-vouches an untrusted needs-info reply; with none waiting it is refused (row 8t).
ready needs a passing gate record at the head (rows 32b and 31).
ready needs a valid review at the head (rows 32c and 31).
ready needs a passing review ledger at the head (rows 32d and 31).
A protected-path violation at the gate parks the job for a person (row 25).
A merge conflict on a protected or config-loading path parks the job for a person (row 33b).
An escalated review parks the job for a person (row 29), after a confirm park when a write needs one.
A trusted foreign marker, or an edited engine marker, parks a ready job (row 38).
A person's push does not re-gate a job while an untrusted edit waits for a retry (rows 52h and 52hs).
A person's push does not re-gate a job whose issue an outsider closed while it stays closed (rows 52h and 52hs).
A person's push re-gates a job that had reached build, whatever stage its park recorded (row 52h).
A push to a job that never reached build is recorded and the job stays (row 52hs).
A retry does not repeat a resolve until the base has moved past conflict_base_sha (row 44xr).
The merge directive's success ends the job as merged (row 64).
A worker that parks on a blocking question moves the job to needs_human (rows 43, 43qr and 44b).
Checks that run past ciTimeoutSeconds park the job for a person (row 63t).
The intake judge's REJECT ends the job as rejected (row 5).
